Aerospace plate, Fairchild and the fab shops: how SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 apply around Spokane

Spokane is not an airframe town the way Everett is, but aerospace reaches more Inland Northwest NDT jobs than people expect. Kaiser Aluminum's Trentwood mill in Spokane Valley moved from can stock to aluminum plate for the aircraft industry, has sold that plate to Boeing under a long-term contract and to Airbus, and added an ultrasonic inspection system as it moved into heavy plate. Fairchild Air Force Base flies the KC-135 tanker. Most of the rest, from Avista's hydro plants to the valley's fabricators, is code work.

Mill product for aircraft: whose rules?

A plate mill sells material rather than finished parts, and it inspects against the material specifications and purchase-order clauses its customers send. Those clauses decide the personnel standard. Where an aerospace customer invokes NAS 410 (or EN 4179 on a European order), the NDT personnel doing that inspection are certified under a NAS 410 program run by a Responsible Level 3 (RL3) designated in writing. Where an order names something else, the written practice follows that instead. Anyone applying for ultrasonic or eddy current work at a mill should ask which customers' clauses the program is written to meet, because one plant can serve aerospace, industrial and transport customers at the same time. Much mill inspection is automated, and NAS 410 has a Level 1 Limited category for people certified to perform one narrowly defined operation; ask whether a role is limited or full Level 1 before you accept it.

Fairchild and the contractors around it

Air Force maintainers at Fairchild work under the service's own directives and technical orders, not under either private-sector document. Contractors who support the base, or who make and repair parts for military aircraft, are another matter: defense aerospace subcontracts commonly carry NAS 410 down from the prime, because NAS 410 replaced MIL-STD-410 on defense contracts in 1998. If you leave the Air Force with aircraft inspection experience, a civilian employer will certify you again, so collect every training record and log you can before you go.

Why most Spokane NDT jobs sit under SNT-TC-1A

Hydro and gas plants, rail and bridge steel, and the machine shops that serve mining, timber and agriculture all work to ASME, AWS, ASTM and owner specifications. Those documents look to ASNT SNT-TC-1A, or to CP-189 where a code names it, so the employer's written practice rests on the ASNT recommended practice, and customers audit that written practice, not SNT-TC-1A directly. A Spokane technician can spend a decade on that work without meeting a NAS 410 clause, then take an aerospace job across the mountains and meet one on the first morning.

If an aerospace job is your next move

  1. Keep course outlines and hour records, not only completion certificates. An RL3 credits evidence, not course titles.
  2. Log experience by method and product form (plate, welds, castings, machined parts) and get it signed as you earn it.
  3. Expect gap training in magnetic particle and penetrant, where NAS 410 asks for more formal training than SNT-TC-1A recommends.
  4. Keep near-vision and color records current; a lapsed vision test can suspend a certification.
  5. Read the NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A comparison before the interview, and the Everett and Seattle pages for the Puget Sound employers.

Remember that an SNT-TC-1A certificate from a Spokane employer does not satisfy a NAS 410 requirement on its own. The records behind it are what a new RL3 can credit.

Atlantis for Spokane employers and technicians

Atlantis brings aerospace and aviation companies here the same offer it brings a utility or a fabricator: ASNT NDT Level III consulting, training based on SNT-TC-1A, and UT, MT, PT and VT inspection. Theory is self-paced online with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions, practice runs in the Practical NDT simulator, and the practical examination takes place at the employer's site. Spokane has no Atlantis classroom. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to Spokane companies. Whether a course will count toward NAS 410 certification is decided by the employer's RL3, and the time to ask is before signing up. For mills and shops getting ready for a customer or Nadcap AC7114 audit, Atlantis prepares NAS 410 audit documentation that the company's own RL3 reviews and approves.
